title: Constructs
description: Artificial things built in the pre-verdant age or the earliest days of new sailing, still performing tasks nobody remembers assigning them.
inPlay: Constructs are predictable in a way beasts are not - they follow programming, however corrupted. Let the crew work out what a construct was built to do; exploiting that purpose is usually the key to surviving it.

hazards.name: Keepers of Secrets Long-Dead
hazards.summary: Towerspiders: not really spiders, but close enough in design, these large constructs perform now-useless maintenance within pre-verdant ruins, bent on protecting something.

hazards.name: Punchcard Pioneers made for the Wavecutting Age
hazards.summary: Bellows-garl: wheezing seafaring constructs built in the earliest days of new sailing to crew ships through spore-filled areas, driven by concertina-like contraptions operating on air throughflow.

hazards.name: Ships Gone Feral on the Open Waves
hazards.summary: Mawships: wildsea vessels gone truly wild - abandoned, never quite claimed by the waves, and refusing to sink, with bites mutated into something hungry.

hazards.name: Mindless Mechanical Menace
hazards.summary: The mad woodcutter: its programming corrupted, it lurches through the canopy on pistoned legs, cutting branches in a mindless echo of its old task.
